title: Flexible and non-invasive passive integrated transponder (PIT) tagging protocols for tropical freshwater fish species
author: Grieve, Lee, et al.
materials: •Biomark HPT12 (single-use) needles pre-loaded with PIT tags (12.5 mm 134.2 kHz ISO FDX-B) (Biomark, Boise, Idaho, USA)•Biomark MK-25 implant gun (Biomark, Boise, Idaho, USA)•Aqui-S anaesthetic (Aqui-S, Lower Hut, New Zealand)•Apparatus capable of weighing anaesthetized fish in grams and measuring them in millimetres.

steps.title: Prepare anesthetic solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve Aqui‑S in water to a concentration of 25 mg L⁻¹.

steps.title: Anesthetize fish
steps.instruction: Immerse each fish in the 25 mg L⁻¹ Aqui‑S solution until loss of equilibrium and a reduced opercular beat rate are observed.

steps.title: Weigh and measure fish
steps.instruction: Record the weight of each anaesthetized fish in grams and its total length in millimetres using appropriate scales and measuring devices.

steps.title: Insert PIT tag
steps.instruction: Using a Biomark MK‑25 implant gun fitted with a pre‑loaded 12.5 mm Biomark HPT12 needle (134.2 kHz ISO FDX‑B), implant the PIT tag into the fish.

steps.title: Fin clip fish
steps.instruction: Clip a small portion of a fin to create a synthetic extrinsic mark that records the fish has received a PIT tag.

steps.title: Recover fish in aerated tank
steps.instruction: Place the tagged and fin‑clipped fish into a 60 L recovery aquarium containing aerated water and monitor until the effects of anaesthesia have fully subsided.

steps.title: Return fish to source
steps.instruction: After full recovery, return each fish to its original holding tank or source environment.
